title: Algebraize a map from a scalar extension, with torsion kernel and cokernel
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and $R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Call an $R$-module $I$-power torsion when for every element $x$ there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that $r x=0$ for every $r\in I^n$; for an $S$-module use restriction of scalars. Let $P$ be an $R$-module and $Q$ an $S$-module; write $S\otimes_R P$ for scalar extension and $\psi_S$ for scalar extension of a linear map [def-weil-module-base-change]. For an $S$-linear map $\varphi:S\otimes_R P\to Q$ with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel, there exist an $R$-module $T$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:P\to T$, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:S\otimes_R T\to Q$ such that $\beta\circ\psi_S=\varphi$, and both $\ker\psi$ and $T/\operatorname{im}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (lemma-application-formal-glueing), proof of part (2), using Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data) and Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence); torsion follows by exact localization and finite generation as in step 5 of lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family $f:\mathrm{Fin}(t)\to R$ for $I$. At each generator prove bijectivity of the localized given map directly on fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For injectivity, if the image of $m/1$ is zero, clear its denominator to get $f^n m\in\ker\varphi$. An ideal power annihilates this kernel element, so a further power of $f$ kills $m$. For surjectivity of $y/s$, annihilate the class of $y$ in the cokernel by $I^n$, lift $f^n y$ to a numerator $m$, and use $m/(f^n s)$. Transport between the restricted and supplied scalar actions by the scalar-tower law.

Use [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] to obtain the fully faithful, essentially surjective canonical functor Can with its specified object and morphism components. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-replace-prime] to $\mathrm{Can}(P)$ and the given map, producing a datum $Y$ with prime component $Q$ and a morphism $\mu:\mathrm{Can}(P)\to Y$ with bijective charts. Essential surjectivity gives $\theta:\mathrm{Can}(T)\simeq Y$. Fullness lifts $\mu\theta^{-1}$ to $\psi:P\to T$. Define $\beta$ to be the prime component of $\theta$, identified with $S\otimes_R T\to Q$. The specified prime-component formula for Can, $\theta\theta^{-1}=1$, and the prime-component equation for $\mu$ give $\beta\psi_S=\varphi$. The chart-component formula for Can makes every $\psi_{f_i}$ bijective.

For $x\in\ker\psi$, injectivity of each localized map makes $x/1=0$. For a cokernel class $[y]$, surjectivity supplies a preimage of $y/1$; applying the localized quotient map gives $[y]/1=0$. The fraction criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] supplies a power of every generator killing the element. Put $J=\ker(R\to M,\ r\mapsto rx)$, its annihilator ideal. Each generator is in $\sqrt J$, hence $I\subseteq\sqrt J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power], Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg, to get $I^n\subseteq J$. This proves both torsion assertions, including the empty-family case.
